title: Influence of the Use of ICT on University Students in Different Cultures After the COVID-19 Pandemic
content:
Background: Once the covid-19 pandemic ended, the abusive use of the internet and new information and communication technologies (ICT) was detected among university students. What has been the impact on the academic performance of university students? How did the pandemic affect students' relationship with ICT’s? The objective of this research was to explore the use of mobile phones and the internet in students from different cultures (Spanish and Japanese) after the pandemic.
Methodology: This is a descriptive and exploratory analysis study in university students (n=206) from Spanish and Japanese culture to understand the perception of academic performance after the covid-19 pandemic, the general use of ICT and the abusive use of both of the internet and the mobile phone. For this study, a semi-structured questionnaire was applied with the scales Internet Over-use Scale (IOS) and Cell-Phone Over (COS).
Results:Almost half of university students use the internet and mobile phones excessively. There are statistically significant differences between students of Spanish and Japanese culture regarding the consequences derived from excessive Internet use and by sex in terms of tolerance of ICT abuse. There are more university students of Japanese culture with excessive use of the Internet compared to those of Spanish culture. And a lower percentage of abusive use of both the Internet and the mobile phone in university men than in women.
Conclusions:Many of the university students use ICT excessively and show signs of pathological addiction. Extreme internet use is related to extreme mobile phone use in this vulnerable group. Abusive use has influenced the habits of university students after the covid-19 pandemic.
